title: Both settings screens, both viewports, at rest: six rows, one eyebrow — and the in-match screen has another button standing on its DONE
attestation: FOUR FRAMES, TWO SURFACES, TWO VIEWPORTS, ALL ON THE PRODUCTION BUNDLE (npm run build + preview) with the build stamp bc4e78f* in the corner of every one. The menu screen was reached by pressing SETTINGS on the main menu; the match screen by PLAY -> PLAY SOLO -> RUSH -> ESC -> SETTINGS, at the physical points the client itself reports drawing those controls at. The pointer was parked off every plate before each shot, so these are the screens at rest. WHAT ALL FOUR SHOW: the header word SETTINGS at top left and the eyebrow CHANGES SAVE IMMEDIATELY at top right; six rows, each led by a `?` square; FIRE MODE with the chip AUTO-AIM, CONTROLS with the chip TAP COMMANDER, REDUCE VFX with the chip OFF, then MASTER VOLUME, SFX VOLUME and MUSIC VOLUME, each a bar of ten pips with a - and a + at the right end. Counted off the frames: master 8 pips lit of 10, sfx 8 of 10, music 6 of 10. On the desktop the six rows are one column; at 798x384 they wrap into two columns of three, toggles left and volumes right, and nothing is clipped or overlapped at that width. THE ONE THING THAT IS WRONG IS ON THE MATCH SURFACE, AND IT IS ON BOTH VIEWPORTS: the match's own DOWNLOAD LOG button is drawn on top of the settings screen's DONE plate in the bottom-right corner. On the phone frame the word DONE is not on the screen at all — the only part of the plate still visible is its left accent bar. On the desktop frame the plate is wider, so DO is readable and the rest of the word is behind DOWNLOAD LOG. That is why this entry's verdict is failed rather than verified, and what a press on it actually does is photographed separately in a0-96-pause-done-is-covered-by-download-log. The match frames also show the frozen world through the overlay — the objective line, the station nameplate, VIEW 1x — which is the pause overlay behaving as designed and is not a finding.

title: The header's claim tested on the desktop: all six rows moved off their defaults come back from a full page reload, and the only pixels that differ are a focus ring
attestation: ONE BROWSER CONTEXT, THREE FRAMES, 1280x800. Frame 1, fresh storage: FIRE MODE AUTO-AIM, CONTROLS TAP COMMANDER, REDUCE VFX OFF, MASTER 8 pips lit of 10, SFX 8 of 10, MUSIC 6 of 10. Then every row was moved off its default by pressing the control a player presses — the three toggle rows once each, and the volume rows on their own - and + buttons (master five times down, sfx twice up, music six times down). Frame 2, same page load: FIRE MODE MANUAL, CONTROLS KEYBOARD + MOUSE, REDUCE VFX ON, MASTER 3 of 10, SFX 10 of 10 (hard against the top), MUSIC 0 of 10 (not one pip lit). Then the page was RELOADED and the screen reopened from the main menu. Frame 3: FIRE MODE MANUAL, CONTROLS KEYBOARD + MOUSE, REDUCE VFX ON, MASTER 3, SFX 10, MUSIC 0. ROW BY ROW, WHAT SURVIVED THE RELOAD: FIRE MODE yes; CONTROLS yes; REDUCE VFX yes; MASTER VOLUME yes; SFX VOLUME yes; MUSIC VOLUME yes. NOTHING WAS LOST. The pip counts are also on the plate as 3x crops of the same two frames, so the numbers can be counted rather than taken on trust. THE TWO FRAMES EITHER SIDE OF THE RELOAD DIFFER BY 1408 PIXELS OF 4096000, and every one of them falls inside a single 92x92 box at (602, 399): the keyboard focus ring on the CONTROLS row's `?`, bright in the frame taken right after the presses and absent in the freshly loaded one. That is a pointer/keyboard affordance, not a row value; no chip, no label and no pip differs anywhere in the frame. MUSIC VOLUME AT ZERO IS THE STRONGEST SINGLE ROW HERE: an empty bar cannot be confused with a default that happened to be re-seated, and it came back empty.

title: The same run at 798x384: every row survives the reload, and the frame after it is byte-identical to the frame before it
attestation: THE NARROWEST SUPPORTED WIDTH, 798x384 LANDSCAPE, DRIVEN WITH REAL TAPS. Frame 1, fresh storage: AUTO-AIM / TAP COMMANDER / OFF / master 8 pips of 10 / sfx 8 of 10 / music 6 of 10. Frame 2, after the same six changes a player would make: MANUAL / STICKS / ON / master 3 / sfx 10 / music 0. (The CONTROLS chip reads STICKS rather than KEYBOARD + MOUSE because this is a touch device and the row names the device in front of the player.) Frame 3, after a full page reload and a fresh trip in through the main menu: MANUAL / STICKS / ON / master 3 / sfx 10 / music 0. ROW BY ROW: FIRE MODE survived; CONTROLS survived; REDUCE VFX survived; MASTER, SFX and MUSIC all survived. NONE WAS LOST. AND THE FRAME AFTER THE RELOAD IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE FRAME BEFORE IT — 0 pixels of 1225728 differ, peak 0 — so on this profile there is nothing at all to argue about: the screen a player comes back to is the same image they left. The 3x crops of the three volume bars are on the plate, before and after, so the 8/8/6 and the 3/10/0 can be counted pip by pip.

title: The second surface reads the same storage: six values set on the menu screen survive a reload AND a fresh match boot, on both viewports
attestation: THE TWO SCREENS HOLD SEPARATE STATE — the match loads its own copy of the settings when it boots — so a frame of the menu screen proves nothing about the match's. This run does the crossing on purpose: change all six rows on the MENU screen, press DONE, RELOAD THE PAGE, then boot a match through the front door (PLAY -> PLAY SOLO -> RUSH) and open pause -> SETTINGS. Nothing in memory survives that reload; whatever is on these two frames was read back out of storage by the match. PHONE 798x384: FIRE MODE MANUAL, CONTROLS STICKS, REDUCE VFX ON, MASTER 3 pips of 10, SFX 10 of 10, MUSIC 0 of 10 — the six values set on the other screen, all six of them. DESKTOP 1280x800: MANUAL, KEYBOARD + MOUSE, ON, 3, 10, 0. Same six. NOT ONE ROW ARRIVED AT ITS DEFAULT. Both frames also carry the DOWNLOAD LOG button on the DONE plate, which is the finding recorded in a0-96-pause-done-is-covered-by-download-log and is not what this entry is about.

title: FIRE MODE under Tap Commander: the chip answers every press and the match frame does not move one pixel — while the same press on the sticks scheme moves 18935 of them
attestation: THE BOOT IS ?debug=1&freeze=1: the sim is advanced to a fixed seeded tick and pinned there, so the match frame is byte-deterministic and the only thing that can differ between two shots of it is what the capture did in between. DESKTOP 1280x800. Frame A, the frozen match with CONTROLS on the shipped default TAP COMMANDER and the chip on AUTO-AIM; the controls strip along the bottom reads 'Click anywhere - Move or attack' and 'Build & Upgrade - get closer to your station'. Frame A re-shot with nothing touched: 0 pixels differ — that is the null, and it is what makes the rest of the numbers mean anything. Then pause -> SETTINGS: the chip reads AUTO-AIM, CONTROLS reads TAP COMMANDER. ONE PRESS ON THE FIRE MODE ROW AND THE CHIP READS MANUAL — the control responds, visibly, immediately. Back to the match at the same pinned tick: 0 PIXELS OF 4096000 DIFFER FROM FRAME A. The strip still says 'Click anywhere - Move or attack'; it does not mention firing or aiming in either state. THE CONTROL THAT PROVES THE MEASUREMENT IS NOT BLIND, taken in the same run and on the same frozen tick: switch CONTROLS to KEYBOARD + MOUSE and press the SAME row. The strip grows a row — 'WASD Thrust | Mouse Aim | Left mouse Fire / Mine' in MANUAL — and loses it again in AUTO-AIM, where it reads 'WASD Thrust | Left mouse Hold to fire / mine - auto-aim picks the target'. 18935 pixels differ between those two. THE PHONE, 798x384, SAYS IT MORE PLAINLY STILL: under TAP COMMANDER the frame carries no thumb furniture at all and the AUTO-AIM and MANUAL frames differ by 0 pixels of 1225728; under STICKS the same toggle swaps the right-hand aim-stick ring for a round FIRE button, 28671 pixels. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SHOW: it shows that on the default control scheme, on both viewports, a press that changes the chip changes nothing that is drawn — including the strip whose whole job is to tell the player what their controls do. It does not, on its own, say what the sim would have done over live ticks; a pinned frame cannot. It is the visible half of the row, and the visible half is what a player has. This is docs/settings.md's mismatch 1, photographed: a control that responds and changes nothing.

title: Every `?` panel photographed as it renders, on both viewports: six explanations, one of which tells the default-scheme player their row does nothing
attestation: EACH PANEL WAS OPENED BY PRESSING THAT ROW'S `?` ON THE MAIN-MENU SETTINGS SCREEN AND PHOTOGRAPHED; the crops on this plate are cut out by difference against the same screen with no panel open, so no rectangle was chosen by hand. READ OFF THE DESKTOP FRAMES, WORD FOR WORD. FIRE MODE: 'TAP COMMANDER aims and fires for you. Switch CONTROLS to aim yourself.' CONTROLS: 'TAP COMMANDER flies the ship for you: tap where to go, tap what to hit. On KEYBOARD + MOUSE you fly it yourself.' REDUCE VFX: 'Thins the effects that carry no information, to hold the frame rate. The game does this on its own when the rate drops; ON keeps them thin all the time.' MASTER VOLUME: 'Every sound the game makes.' SFX VOLUME: 'Weapons, impacts, engines, menus.' MUSIC VOLUME: 'The soundtrack.' THE PHONE FRAMES CARRY THE SAME SIX SENTENCES with exactly one difference, and it is the right one: CONTROLS names the device in front of the player, so at 798x384 it reads 'On STICKS you fly it yourself'. Every panel is titled with its own row's name and floats clear of the row it describes and of that row's value. A SEVENTH FRAME IS ON THE PLATE because the same `?` says two different things: with CONTROLS switched to KEYBOARD + MOUSE, FIRE MODE's panel reads 'AUTO-AIM locks the nearest target and leads it while you fire. MANUAL leaves the aim to you.' One row, the same word on its chip, two accounts of what it does — the panel is honest about the row being dead on the default scheme, which is the thing the chip itself does not say. ONE COSMETIC OBSERVATION, NOT A FAILURE: at 798x384 the FIRE MODE panel's top edge covers the screen's own SETTINGS title. Nothing of the panel is clipped by the viewport and nothing it explains is hidden by it.

title: The in-match settings screen's DONE is under the match's DOWNLOAD LOG button: a press on the plate's own centre saves a log file and leaves the screen up, on both viewports
attestation: FOUND BY LOOKING AT THE FIRST IN-MATCH FRAME, THEN PROVED WITH A PRESS. Front-door boot, offline match, ESC -> SETTINGS. In the bottom-right corner the match's own DOWNLOAD LOG button is drawn on top of the settings screen's DONE plate. On the phone crop (798x384, magnified 2x) the word DONE is not on the screen at all — what is left of the plate is its left end and its accent bar, running out from under a blue-bordered button that says DOWNLOAD LOG. On the desktop crop the plate is wider, so DO is readable and the rest of the word is behind the same button. THEN THE PRESS. At the point the client ITSELF reports drawing DONE at — (646.5, 359.5) css on the phone, (1086, 754) on the desktop — one press: the seam read `settings` before it and `settings` after it, ON BOTH VIEWPORTS. The screen did not close. What did happen is in the frame: the button now reads LOG SAVED above the line 'Log saved to your downloads — attach that file.', and the browser received a file — planet-rush-log-bc4e78f-20260819-091630.json on the phone, a second one at 091654 on the desktop. A player pressing the only way off this screen gets a diagnostic download instead. HOW BAD IT IS, MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED: the way out is not gone. A press further left — (541.5, 359.5) on the phone, (986, 754) on the desktop, both on the part of the plate the button does not cover — reaches DONE: the pause menu comes back (PAUSED / RESUME / SETTINGS / EXIT TO MENU) and nothing is downloaded. So DONE answers only at the end of the plate that carries no label, while its centre and its word belong to another button. On the desktop, ESC also backs out. ONE HONEST NOTE ON THIS RUN: the desktop leg was pressed twice. The first attempt, at (921, 754), missed the plate's left edge by 13 css px and closed nothing and downloaded nothing — an inconclusive press, not a finding, and the offset was corrected and re-run. THE FRAME OF THE SUCCESSFUL LEFT-END PRESS CARRIES BUILD STAMP 5992ca4* WHERE THE OTHERS CARRY bc4e78f*: the same game code rebuilt after this directory's capture harness was committed — `git diff bc4e78f..5992ca4 -- src/` is empty.
